text:
Anya Velasquez: Heads up — we've got a burst of 429s for org:acme right now. Dashboard shows enforcement rejections ~2m before the usage appears in metering. :thinking:
Samuel Choi: Seen that pattern before — enforcement reads from the real-time token cache which is populated by the usage consumer. If the consumer lags, enforcement can undercount and start rejecting. Are we seeing consumer lag or delayed producer acks?
Dima Petrov: Consumer lag. Kafka consumer group enforcer-consumers shows partition skew on shard-7. throughput down and GC spikes in the consumer pods.
Lisa Ng: Any quick mitigation to stop customer impact? Can we relax the burst policy for affected orgs or disable enforcement temporarily?
prod-oncall: I can temporarily add acme org to the enforcement whitelist for 15m to stop the 429s. Doing that now — will post when done.
billing-bot: [automated] alert: enforcement.rejections.org=acme count=342 window=60s severity=warning link=https://console/redwood/alerts/ENF-342
Anya Velasquez: Thanks. Even with a whitelist we need root cause — we can't keep whitelisting. Dima, can you dump the consumer lag and offsets?
Dima Petrov: Pasted consumer state (trimmed):
```
Group: enforcer-consumers
Partition: shard-7  lag: 124k  current_offset: 4821934  end_offset: 4946134
Pod: enforcer-consumer-7  last_gc: 23s  cpu: 88%
```
Looks like we fell behind during a spike around 11:04 UTC.
Samuel Choi: Spike correlates with a large batch import from customers S3 (ingest-producer). Producer emitted ~1.2M events in 30s, consumer parallelism (replicas=3) couldn't keep up. Our enforcement cache TTL is short so token refill is tied to consumer progress.
Lisa Ng: Short-term: increase consumer replicas to 6 and bump max.poll.records to 2000. Also increase enforcement cache grace window to 60s so slight ingestion jitter won't immediately trigger rejects.
Anya Velasquez: Agreed. Also we should decouple enforcement from being strictly driven by the metering consumer. Idea: maintain a lightweight realtime counter in Redis populated by a separate high-priority stream consumer that only processes per-org counts (no heavy enrichment). It would be a soft real-time source for enforcement and still reconcile from full metering later. Thoughts?
Dima Petrov: That would help. Implementation notes: use compacted Kafka topic with per-org deltas, stateless micro-consumer that does INCRBY on Redis per-org and emits checkpoint offsets. Enforcer reads Redis for token bucket fill level. Reconciliation job subtracts Redis-derived counts from final metering to detect drift.
Samuel Choi: Two cautions: 1) Need strong idempotency/dedup keys on the delta stream to avoid double-counting if the consumer retries. 2) Redis as source of truth for enforceable counts means we need replication and bandaid for failover. Prefer using Redis streams with consumer groups + monotonic checkpoints.
Lisa Ng: Also add observable metrics: enforcement.read_source, enforcement.read_latency, enforcement.fallback_count. Right now we have virtually no metric that says "enforcement used cache vs metering DB."
Anya Velasquez: Action items:
- Dima to scale consumers and implement the short-term grace window (hotfix) — ETA 30m
- Dima to spin up a spike-consumer runbook to drain backlog safely (runbook PR) — ETA EOD
- Samuel to draft design doc for Redis per-org delta stream + reconciliation job — ETA tomorrow morning
- Lisa to add enforcement source metrics and dashboard panel (alerts if enforcement falls back to stale counts) — ETA today
- Prod-oncall to monitor and revert whitelist after consumer catches up
prod-oncall: Whitelist added. Observability: 429 rate dropped immediately after whitelist. Monitoring consumer scale now.
billing-bot: [automated] event: consumer.scale replicas=6 reason=manual-change by=dima link=https://k8s/redwood/enforcer/scale
Dima Petrov: Scaling done. Starting backlog drain. Will post offsets after 5m.
Anya Velasquez: Thanks all. Long-term we should consider making enforcement configurable: prefer "metering-backed" (strong accuracy) vs "realtime-estimate" (lower latency, allow small overage). That would give product teams more control.
Samuel Choi: +1 and add a canary flag to toggle behavior per-tenant. We can roll realtime-estimate only to low-risk tenants first.
Lisa Ng: I'll sketch the dashboard UX for that flag and tie it to rollout controls.
Anya Velasquez: OK closing the triage — we'll follow up in a design doc thread. Leaving the slack thread open for updates. :eyes:
